title: Specialization of a relative associated point at a flat fibre-component generic point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. For $s\in S$ let $X_s$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $i_s:X_s\to X$ its projection and $\mathcal F_s=i_s^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. A point $x\in X_s$ is an associated point of $\mathcal F_s$ if the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is an associated prime [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes] of the stalk $(\mathcal F_s)_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] as an $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$-module. The relative assassin $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ is the set of points $x\in X$ which, regarded as points of $X_{f(x)}$, are associated points of $\mathcal F_{f(x)}$. $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ at $x\in X$ if the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is a flat $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}$-module [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Let $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ and put $t=f(y)$. Let $Y=\overline{\{y\}}\subseteq X$ with its reduced integral closed-subscheme structure [def-pc-integral-scheme]. For $s\in S$, let $Y_s$ denote the fibre of the composite $Y\to X\to S$. Let $C$ be an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $Y_s$, and let $x$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point], viewed as a point of $X$. Assume only that $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ at this point $x$. Then $x\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ and $\dim_x(Y_s)=\dim C=\dim(Y_t)$, where $\dim$ is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and $\dim_x$ is local topological dimension [def-kun-dimension].

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), statement and proof, second paragraph: the equality of the dimension of C with that of C′ and Y_t.

proof.text: Take the valuative diagram, points $y',x'$ and $Y'$ of [lem-trf-valuative-fibre-component-lift]. Closed immersions and composition preserve local finite type, and so does base change; hence $Y\to S$, $X'\to S'$ and $Y'\to S'$ are locally of finite type. The reduced closure $Y'$ lies in $Y\times_SS'$, since its defining ideal vanishes at $y'$ and hence in the domain of every nonempty affine chart. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$, and let $C'$ be the component of $Y'_{s'}$ with generic point $x'$. The integral $Y'$ dominates $S'$ because its generic point $y'$ maps to $t'$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), assembly step 1; split of the three proof paragraphs.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal F'=(g')^*\mathcal F$; pullback preserves quasi-coherence and finite type. The pullback stalk formula and pointwise relative flat extension make $\mathcal F'_{x'}$ flat over $A$. In the field extension $Y_t\times_t t'$, $y'$ is component generic over $y$, which is generic in the integral $Y_t$: over an affine base chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$, a nonempty domain chart $D$ of $Y$ has kernel $\mathfrak t$ in $R$, so the cited localization lemma applies to $R/\mathfrak t\hookrightarrow D$. The residue field of $y$ is unchanged by $Y_t\hookrightarrow X_t$, so the residual-component lemma makes $y'$ residual generic for $X_t$ too; relative-assassin base change gives $y'\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X'/S'}(\mathcal F')$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), assembly step 2; split of the three proof paragraphs.

proof.text: Apply the stalk-model lemma to $X',\mathcal F',y',x'$. Its local map $A\to B$ is essentially of finite type, $N=\mathcal F'_{x'}$ is finite, $\mathfrak q\cap A=0$, and $\sqrt{\mathfrak q+\mathfrak m_AB}=\mathfrak m_B$; its generic-fibre stalk has associated maximal ideal by step 2. The local-algebra specialization lemma, using the $A$-flatness of $N$, gives $\mathfrak m_R\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(L)$. The model identifies this with $x'\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X'/S'}(\mathcal F')$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), assembly step 3; split of the three proof paragraphs.

proof.text: Relative-assassin base change now gives $x\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ and residual genericity of $x'$. The residual fibre is unchanged by $Y_s\hookrightarrow X_s$, whose residue field at $x$ is unchanged. The residual-component lemma applied to $Y_s$ shows that $x'$ is component generic in $Y_s\times_s s'$; its closure there equals $C'$ in the closed subscheme $Y'_{s'}$. Applied at $y'$, the same lemma identifies its component in $Y_t\times_t t'$ with the underlying $Y'_{t'}$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), assembly step 4; split of the three proof paragraphs.

proof.text: The fibres $Y_s,Y_t$ are locally of finite type over their fields by base change. The integral valuation-scheme dimension lemma gives $\dim C'=\dim Y'_{t'}$. The field-extension component/local-dimension comparison gives $\dim C'=\dim_xY_s$ and $\dim Y'_{t'}=\dim_yY_t=\dim Y_t$. For the identity field extension it also gives $\dim C=\dim_xY_s$. Together these yield $\dim_xY_s=\dim C=\dim Y_t$, completing both conclusions.

lean.statement: theorem flat_relative_associated_specialization {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (y : X) (hy : y ∈ Scheme.Modules.relativeAssassin f F) (s : S) (C : Set ((f.associatedPointClosureToBase y).fiber s)) (hC : C ∈ irreducibleComponents ((f.associatedPointClosureToBase y).fiber s)) (x : (f.associatedPointClosureToBase y).fiber s) (hx : IsGenericPoint x C) (hflat : Module.Flat (S.presheaf.stalk (f (f.associatedPointClosureFiberToAmbient y s x))) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (f.stalkMap (f.associatedPointClosureFiberToAmbient y s x)).hom).obj ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (f.associatedPointClosureFiberToAmbient y s x)).obj F))) : f.associatedPointClosureFiberToAmbient y s x ∈ Scheme.Modules.relativeAssassin f F ∧ topologicalKrullDimAt x = topologicalKrullDim C ∧ topologicalKrullDim C = topologicalKrullDim ((f.associatedPointClosureToBase y).fiber (f y))
